"mode": 0, "inputs": [], "outputs": [], "properties": {}, "widgets_values": ["If you don't have much VRAM, you probably need to either stick with tiled upscale (or ignore 2a and 2b completely), or play around with optimizations like blocks_to_swap and tile_size. You could also try different versions of SeedVR:
3b fp8 requires ~3.3 Gb VRAM. 3b Q4 - even less.
7b Q4 requires ~4.5 Gb VRAM.
7b fp16 requires ~16 Gb VRAM.

I'd suggest you to avoid the "sharp" variant as in my tests it was quiet bad and not exactly "sharp".

There is a setting called "shorter_edge". It downscales your image so that the shorter edge of it is equal to the value you've set. "WHY TF DO WE DO THAT?" you'd ask. Well, SeedVR does it magic best when it upscales a smaller image. It's a very clever upscaler, unlike the more classic ESRGAN models.
BUT! The upscaler obviously wasn't trained on a ton of adult content. If you downscale too aggressively, anatomy like nipples or genitalia can lose their shape. If your "bits" are looking a bit messy, just bump the "shorter_edge" value up. You'll lose a little bit of that SeedVR upscale "magic," but the details will stay much cleaner."], "color": "#432", "bgcolor": "#653"}, {"id": 67, "type": "Note", "pos": [5330, 920], "size": [350, 190], "flags": {"pinned": true}, "order": 14, "mode": 4, "inputs": [], "outputs": [], "properties": {"widget_ue_connectable": {}}, "widgets_values": ["the skin enhancing model can be downloaded there

3b fp8 requires ~3.3 Gb VRAM. 3b Q4 - even less.
7b Q4 requires ~4.5 Gb VRAM.
7b fp16 requires ~16 Gb VRAM.

I'd suggest you to avoid the "sharp" variant as in my tests it was quiet bad and not exactly "sharp".

There is a setting called "shorter_edge". It downscales your image so that the shorter edge of it is equal to the value you've set. "WHY TF DO WE DO THAT?" you'd ask. Well, SeedVR does it magic best when it upscales a smaller image. It's a very clever upscaler, unlike the more classic ESRGAN models.
BUT! The upscaler obviously wasn't trained on a ton of adult content. If you downscale too aggressively, anatomy like nipples or genitalia can lose their shape. (or ignore 2a and 2b completely), or play around with optimizations like blocks_to_swap and tile_size. You could also try different versions of SeedVR:
3b fp8 requires ~3.3 Gb VRAM. 3b Q4 - even less.
7b Q4 requires ~4.5 Gb VRAM.
7b fp16 requires ~16 Gb VRAM.

I'd suggest you to avoid the "sharp" variant as in my tests it was quiet bad and not exactly "sharp".

There is a setting called "shorter_edge". It downscales your image so that the shorter edge of it is equal to the value you've set. "WHY TF DO WE DO THAT?" you'd ask. Well, SeedVR does it magic best when it upscales a smaller image. It's a very clever upscaler, unlike the more classic ESRGAN models.
BUT! The upscaler obviously wasn't trained on a ton of adult content. If you downscale too aggressively, anatomy like nipples or genitalia can lose their shape. If your "bits" are looking a bit messy, just bump the "shorter_edge" value up. "mode": 0, "inputs": [], "outputs": [], "properties": {}, "widgets_values": ["If you don't have much VRAM, you probably need to either stick with tiled upscale (or ignore 2a and 2b completely), or play around with optimizations like blocks_to_swap and tile_size. You could also try different versions of SeedVR:
3b fp8 requires ~3.3 Gb VRAM. 3b Q4 - even less.
7b Q4 requires ~4.5 Gb VRAM.
7b fp16 requires ~16 Gb VRAM.

I'd suggest you to avoid the "sharp" variant as in my tests it was quiet bad and not exactly "sharp".

There is a setting called "shorter_edge". It downscales your image so that the shorter edge of it is equal to the value you've set. "WHY TF DO WE DO THAT?" you'd ask. Well, SeedVR does it magic best when it upscales a smaller image. It's a very clever upscaler, unlike the more classic ESRGAN models.
BUT! The upscaler obviously wasn't trained on a ton of adult content. If you downscale too aggressively, anatomy like nipples or genitalia can lose their shape. If your "bits" are looking a bit messy, just bump the "shorter_edge" value up. "mode": 0, "inputs": [], "outputs": [], "properties": {}, "widgets_values": ["If you don't have much VRAM, you probably need to either stick with tiled upscale (or ignore 2a and 2b completely), or play around with optimizations like blocks_to_swap and tile_size. You could also try different versions of SeedVR:
3b fp8 requires ~3.3 Gb VRAM. 3b Q4 - even less.
7b Q4 requires ~4.5 Gb VRAM.
7b fp16 requires ~16 Gb VRAM.

I'd suggest you to avoid the "sharp" variant as in my tests it was quiet bad and not exactly "sharp".

There is a setting called "shorter_edge". It downscales your image so that the shorter edge of it is equal to the value you've set. "WHY TF DO WE DO THAT?" you'd ask. Well, SeedVR does it magic best when it upscales a smaller image. It's a very clever upscaler, unlike the more classic ESRGAN models.
BUT! The upscaler obviously wasn't trained on a ton of adult content. If you downscale too aggressively, anatomy like nipples or genitalia can lose their shape. If your "bits" are looking a bit messy, just bump the "shorter_edge" value up. play around with optimizations like blocks_to_swap and tile_size. You could also try different versions of SeedVR:
3b fp8 requires ~3.3 Gb VRAM. 3b Q4 - even less.
7b Q4 requires ~4.5 Gb VRAM.
7b fp16 requires ~16 Gb VRAM.

I'd suggest you to avoid the "sharp" variant as in my tests it was quiet bad and not exactly "sharp".

There is a setting called "shorter_edge". It downscales your image so that the shorter edge of it is equal to the value you've set. "WHY TF DO WE DO THAT?" you'd ask. Well, SeedVR does it magic best when it upscales a smaller image. It's a very clever upscaler, unlike the more classic ESRGAN models.
BUT! The upscaler obviously wasn't trained on a ton of adult content. If you downscale too aggressively, anatomy like nipples or genitalia can lose their shape. If your "bits" are looking a bit messy, just bump the "shorter_edge" value up.
